jurisdiction.name: United Arab Emirates
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: The UAE governs AI through a mix of federal soft law, sector rules and emirate-level instruments, without an AI-specific federal statute. The National Strategy for AI 2031 (2018), the AI Ethics Principles (2022) and the UAE Charter for the Development and Use of AI (2024) set the national direction; the Personal Data Protection Law (2021) provides the main binding federal layer. Sector regulators add more specific rules: the Central Bank's AI/ML guidance note (2026), the joint financial regulators' enabling-technologies guidelines (2021), and the Cyber Security Council's National Cyber Security Policy for AI. Dubai and Abu Dhabi regulate AI in health (DHA 2021; DoH 2018 and 2025), and the DIFC binds AI-based processing of personal data through Regulation 10 (2023). The direction is consolidation: in June 2026 a Federal Authority for AI and Data was announced to merge the AI Office, TDRA's digital government sector and the Emirates Data Office.
lead_institutions: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain
Federal Authority for Artificial Intelligence and Data (announced June 2026)
Abu Dhabi Artificial Intelligence and Advanced Technology Council
narrative.review_notes: Deep review 2026-10-06 including an emirate-level pass (Dubai, Abu Dhabi, DIFC). ai.gov.ae and csc.gov.ae block automated reading; metadata for the Cyber Security Council AI policy taken from the u.ae policy page. Not recorded: Responsible Metaverse Self-governance Framework and Blockchain Guide (not AI governance); Dubai Law No. 9 of 2023 on autonomous vehicles and ADGM Data Protection Regulations 2021 (to add in a sectoral follow-up); AI Maturity Self-Assessment Tool (tool, not a document). Standards: no UAE national adoption of ISO/IEC 42001 or 5339 found. Several items are held as leads pending an official document.

instruments.official_title: The UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Published on the UAE Legislation platform (policy section), dated 10 June 2024. A principles charter; no binding effect stated.
instruments.summary: Sets 12 principles for developing and using AI in the UAE, including human-machine ties, safety, algorithmic fairness, data privacy, transparency, human oversight, governance and accountability, and inclusive access. Applies as a national reference for government, industry and society; it does not create enforceable obligations.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing ethics, government-governance.
metadata_gaps: Lead entity not named on the policy page

instruments.official_title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
instruments.english_title: UAE National Strategy for Artificial Intelligence 2031
instruments.issuing_authority: Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.publisher_name: Office of the Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Published national strategy (document dated 2018, announced at the World Government Summit). Remains the reference strategy cited by later instruments.
instruments.summary: National strategy to make the UAE a global AI leader by 2031. It sets eight objectives: building reputation as an AI destination, deploying AI in priority sectors, growing the AI ecosystem, adopting AI in government services, attracting and training talent, research capability, data and infrastructure, and AI governance and regulation.
metadata_gaps: Exact launch date not stated in the document

instruments.official_title: UAE's International Stance on Artificial Intelligence Policy
instruments.english_title: UAE's International Stance on Artificial Intelligence Policy
instruments.current_status: Published on the UAE Legislation platform (policy section), dated 2 September 2024.
instruments.summary: States the UAE's position on AI internationally through six principles: advancement, collaboration, community, ethics, sustainability and safety. Frames how the UAE engages on AI governance with other countries and international bodies; no binding obligations.

instruments.issuing_authority: UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain
instruments.publisher_name: UAE Council for Artificial Intelligence and Blockchain
instruments.current_status: Published guidance (December 2022), Creative Commons licensed; listed as the 'AI Ethics Guide' on the government AI resources page.
instruments.summary: Sets eight principles (fairness, accountability, transparency, explainability, robustness, human-centred design, sustainability, privacy) for AI systems that make or inform significant decisions. Gives practical guidelines for public and private developers and operators; voluntary.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing ethics, risk-assurance.

instruments.official_title: AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
instruments.english_title: AI Adoption Guideline in Government Services
instruments.issuing_authority: Ministry of Cabinet Affairs, Prime Minister's Office
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry of Cabinet Affairs, Prime Minister's Office
instruments.current_status: Published guidance; year from the AI Office publications listing (the document itself is undated).
instruments.summary: Framework for federal and other government entities to adopt AI in public services across five maturity stages, from Explorer to Transformer. Covers strategy, use-case selection, data, infrastructure, talent and governance, with emphasis on ethical use and human-machine collaboration.

instruments.official_title: 100 Practical Applications and Use Cases of Generative AI
instruments.english_title: 100 Practical Applications and Use Cases of Generative AI
instruments.issuing_authority: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
instruments.publisher_name: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
instruments.summary: Government guide to generative AI tools and 100 use cases for individuals, businesses and employees. Includes responsible-use advice: protect personal data, verify output reliability, keep human review before relying on generated content.

instruments.official_title: The Practical Applications of Generative AI in Media: 100 Use Cases and Applications
instruments.english_title: 100 Practical Applications and Use Cases of Generative AI in Media
instruments.issuing_authority: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
instruments.publisher_name: UAE Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications Office
instruments.current_status: Published guide (September 2023), prepared with the Dubai Media Council and Dubai Press Club.
instruments.summary: Sector guide on generative AI for media professionals, covering 100 applications in content creation, video, voice and transcription. Recommends human oversight of AI output and attention to privacy and reliability; non-binding.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing generative-ai, sectoral.

instruments.summary: Public guide explaining how AI-generated deepfake audio and video are made and the harms they can cause, including misinformation, cyberbullying and reputational damage. Gives practical ways to detect deepfakes and protect against misuse.

instruments.official_title: Federal Decree by Law No. (45) of 2021 Concerning the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.english_title: Personal Data Protection Law (Federal Decree-Law No. 45 of 2021)
instruments.current_status: Active per the UAE Legislation platform. Issued 20 September 2021; Official Gazette No. 712 (supplement), 26 September 2021; effective 2 January 2022. Arabic text is authoritative.
instruments.summary: Federal data protection law governing the processing of personal data by controllers and processors in the UAE, outside the financial free zones, which have their own regimes. It is the main binding federal law for personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing data-privacy, binding-law.

instruments.official_title: The National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.english_title: National Cyber Security Policy for Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Version 1.1 published by the Cyber Security Council; the u.ae policy page lists it (page updated 2 July 2026). The PDF on csc.gov.ae blocks automated access, so the exact date and binding wording were not read from the document.
instruments.summary: Sets minimum security requirements for adopting AI in the UAE: governance, infrastructure safeguards, protection of algorithms and models, operational safety, threat monitoring and performance evaluation. Calls for human oversight of critical decisions and incident response for AI systems.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing cyber-security, risk-assurance.
metadata_gaps: Binding effect to confirm from the document

instruments.official_title: Guidance Note on the Consumer Protection and Responsible Adoption and Use of Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning by Licensed Financial Institutions in the U.A.E.
instruments.english_title: CBUAE Guidance Note on Responsible Adoption and Use of AI/ML by Licensed Financial Institutions
instruments.current_status: Issued 11 February 2026 per the CBUAE Rulebook; announced 23 February 2026. Framed as guidance principles.
instruments.summary: Sets expectations for all CBUAE-licensed financial institutions, including insurers, using AI and machine learning: board accountability, bias testing and fair outcomes, plain-language disclosure in Arabic and English for high-impact decisions, human oversight models, monitoring and third-party due diligence. To be read with the UAE AI Charter and existing CBUAE standards.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing sectoral, risk-assurance, transparency.

instruments.official_title: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies
instruments.english_title: Guidelines for Financial Institutions Adopting Enabling Technologies
instruments.issuing_authority: Central Bank of the UAE (CBUAE), Securities and Commodities Authority, Dubai Financial Services Authority, ADGM Financial Services Regulatory Authority
instruments.current_status: Jointly issued 15 November 2021 by the four UAE financial regulators.
instruments.summary: Joint principles and best practices for financial institutions licensed by any of the four regulators when adopting APIs, big data analytics and AI, biometrics, cloud computing and distributed ledgers. Aim: safe and sound adoption, with risks from innovation managed proactively.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing sectoral, risk-assurance.

instruments.official_title: Smart Dubai AI Ethics Principles & Guidelines
instruments.english_title: Dubai AI Ethics Principles and Guidelines
instruments.current_status: Principles version 1.6 and Guidelines version 1.11, both dated 30 December 2018. Voluntary.
instruments.summary: Dubai's AI ethics framework: four principles (ethical, secure, humane, inclusive) with detailed guidelines on fairness, accountability, transparency and explainability for AI systems that make significant decisions. Addressed to developers and operators in the public and private sectors; voluntary.

instruments.official_title: Artificial Intelligence in the Healthcare (Policy HISHD/PP-09)
instruments.english_title: DHA Policy for Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
instruments.current_status: Policy HISHD/PP-09, issue 01: issued 1 July 2021, effective 1 October 2021.
instruments.summary: Applies to DHA-licensed facilities and professionals, AI developers using Dubai patient data, and insurers and manufacturers deploying AI in Dubai. Requires AI in healthcare to be safe, secure and supervised by end users, and developers to disclose AI-enabled functions, validation methods, datasets and algorithm types.

instruments.official_title: Regulation 10 on Processing Personal Data through Autonomous and Semi-autonomous Systems (DIFC Data Protection Regulations)
instruments.english_title: DIFC Data Protection Regulations: Regulation 10 (AI and autonomous systems)
instruments.current_status: Enacted and effective 1 September 2023 as part of the amended DIFC Data Protection Regulations. Accreditation and certification frameworks published alongside.
instruments.summary: Binding rules for organisations in the Dubai International Financial Centre that process personal data through AI and other autonomous or semi-autonomous systems. Built on principles, ethics and governance, with an accreditation and certification route through approved bodies.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing data-privacy, binding-law, transparency.

instruments.official_title: Policy on Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the Healthcare Sector of the Emirate of Abu Dhabi
instruments.english_title: DoH Abu Dhabi Policy on Use of AI in Healthcare
instruments.current_status: Policy/AI/0.9, issued and effective 30 April 2018. Compliance is mandatory, with sanctions available.
instruments.summary: Requires healthcare providers, manufacturers, insurers and researchers using Abu Dhabi patient data for AI to keep governance structures, seek recognised certification, report incidents and design systems to degrade safely. Clinicians keep decision-making authority over AI-assisted recommendations.

instruments.english_title: DoH Abu Dhabi Responsible AI Standard
instruments.current_status: Standard DoH/ST/DDGO/RAI/V1/2025, version 1, October 2025. Applies to DoH and all licensed healthcare entities in Abu Dhabi.
instruments.summary: Sets minimum requirements for developing, procuring and deploying AI in Abu Dhabi healthcare across four domains: core principles (safety, fairness, transparency, accountability), data management, risk assessment and mitigation, and AI literacy. Binds DoH and all licensed healthcare entities in the emirate.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Primary-source material for assessing sectoral, risk-assurance.
